subject: Thin-plate splines (GAM) in TMB: high memory usage

messages.author: 9721e69203f06751
messages.subject: Thin-plate splines (GAM) in TMB: high memory usage
parts:
Hello,

I have a question about how memory usage can be reduced when fitting smoothers with many basis dimensions. I'm working with a large spatial dataset (20000 points) and I'm using a thin-plate spline with 60 basis dimensions from mgcv:

gam(y ~ s(easting,northing,bs='ts',k=60))

Here's a simple version of the model code:

#include <TMB.hpp>   //Links in the TMB libraries
template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() (){
  using namespace density;
  using namespace Eigen; //Needed for sparse structures
 
  //2-D GAM
 
  //Read data from R------------------
  DATA_VECTOR(yield);                 // Response
  DATA_MATRIX(smoothMat);             // Design matrix (basis dimensions with no intercept)
  DATA_SPARSE_MATRIX(penaltyMat);     // Sparse penalty matrix from mgcv
  DATA_INTEGER(penaltyDim);           // Dimensions of penalty matrix
 
  //Read parameters from R------------
  PARAMETER(b0);                      // Intercept
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(smoothCoefs);      // Smooth coefficients
  PARAMETER(log_lambda);              // Log penalization parameter
  PARAMETER(log_sigma);               // log(SD) of measurement error
 
  //Transform SD and penalization parameters
  Type sigma = exp(log_sigma);
  Type lambda = exp(log_lambda);
 
  //Initialize objective function
  Type nll=0;
 
  // Penalization part ------------------------------------
 
  //Uses penalization approach from pSplines.cpp (tmb_case_studies)
  SparseMatrix<Type> S = lambda*penaltyMat; //Penalty term * Penalty matrix
  nll -= 0.5*penaltyDim*log_lambda - 0.5*GMRF(S).Quadform(smoothCoefs);
 
  // Main model -------------------------------------------
  vector<Type> mu = b0 + smoothMat*smoothCoefs; //Expected value: mu = Intercept + model matrix %*% coefs
 
  nll -= sum(dnorm(yield, mu, sigma, true)); //Decrement logLik
 
  return nll; //Return likelihood
}

This model fits, but during the first run of obj$fn() the Optimizing Tape routine the memory usage spikes to about 16GB. Is there any way to reduce this? I've managed to fit similar spatial models in TMB using the R-INLA mesh approach, but they never have the same problems with memory usage.

Thanks,
Sam R

messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Thin-plate splines (GAM) in TMB: high memory usage
parts:
Hi,

I suspect that the large memory use is due to "model matrix %*% coefs",
and not the penalty term (dim 60 is not large). You can check if 
I am right by reducing the number of observations, but keeping the number of basis functions.

The only way around this problem that I see is to feed the observations
in batches to the objective function. You then need to write
an R-wrapper that accumulates the objective and gradient values.
There are various ways of implementing this on the c++ side. One
simple is to add "start" and "stop" arguments to determine a batch.
(The penalty should of course only be calculated once, for instance when start==0)

Hans

  using namespace Eigen; //Needed for sparse structures
 
  //2-D GAM
 
  //Read data from R------------------
  DATA_VECTOR(yield);                 // Response
  DATA_MATRIX(smoothMat);             // Design matrix (basis dimensions with no intercept)
  DATA_SPARSE_MATRIX(penaltyMat);     // Sparse penalty matrix from mgcv
  DATA_INTEGER(penaltyDim);           // Dimensions of penalty matrix
 
  //Read parameters from R------------
  PARAMETER(b0);                      // Intercept
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(smoothCoefs);      // Smooth coefficients
  PARAMETER(log_lambda);              // Log penalization parameter
  PARAMETER(log_sigma);               // log(SD) of measurement error
 
  //Transform SD and penalization parameters
  Type sigma = exp(log_sigma);
  Type lambda = exp(log_lambda);
 
  //Initialize objective function
  Type nll=0;
 
  // Penalization part ------------------------------------
 
  //Uses penalization approach from pSplines.cpp (tmb_case_studies)
  SparseMatrix<Type> S = lambda*penaltyMat; //Penalty term * Penalty matrix
  nll -= 0.5*penaltyDim*log_lambda - 0.5*GMRF(S).Quadform(smoothCoefs);
 
  // Main model -------------------------------------------
  vector<Type> mu = b0 + smoothMat*smoothCoefs; //Expected value: mu = Intercept + model matrix %*% coefs
 
  nll -= sum(dnorm(yield, mu, sigma, true)); //Decrement logLik
 
  return nll; //Return likelihood
}

This model fits, but during the first run of obj$fn() the Optimizing Tape routine the memory usage spikes to about 16GB. Is there any way to reduce this? I've managed to fit similar spatial models in TMB using the R-INLA mesh approach, but they never have the same problems with memory usage.

Thanks,
Sam R

parts:
Nice idea, but I'm sorry to say that it doesn't work (unless I'm overlooking something... I hope I am!).

You cannot apply Laplace for each batch and then sum up because
log( integrate exp(f1(u)+f2(u)) du )
is not in general equal to
log( integrate exp(f1(u)) du ) + log( integrate exp(f2(u)) du )

Hardly relevant if the approach doesn't work, but pay special attention to this line of the DATA_UPDATE documentation:
"Updatable data items behave like parameters. In particular, if-else branching on such data should be avoided."
which means that the branch:
if(usePenalty==1){ ... }
won't behave as expected when 'usePenalty' is updated.
